question.text: Low Frequency Algo in commodity markets is defined as:

answer.text: An algorithm with order frequency of 10 OPS (Orders Per Second) or less
An algorithm that trades once per day
An algorithm with more than 10 OPS
Any algorithm that uses limit orders only

explanation.text: The Logic: The framework on page 124 defines Low Frequency Algo as <= 10 OPS, with a generic Algo ID. High Frequency Algo is > 10 OPS and requires registration via the broker. The Trap: "Low frequency" does not mean once per day, > 10 OPS is High Frequency, and order type by itself does not determine the frequency classification. Note: Page 125 attaches Research Analyst registration specifically to black-box algo providers, not to all HFT algo providers, so that nuance is preserved rather than generalised.
